subject: Computer Networking
title: Intrusion Detection Systems
description: A short lesson to help you apply Intrusion Detection Systems.

hook.text: A firewall blocks known threats. But what about attacks that slip through? An IDS watches for suspicious behavior.

buildup.text: An IDS monitors network traffic for patterns that match known attack signatures or unusual behavior.

discovery.text: Signature-based detection matches known attacks. Anomaly-based flags anything deviating from normal behavior.

twist.text: An IDS only alerts — it doesn't block. An IPS goes further by automatically dropping malicious traffic.

climax.text: Modern systems combine both approaches. Machine learning helps identify new attack patterns never seen before.

punchline.text: Firewalls are the lock. IDS is the alarm system.

quiz.question: What is the difference between an IDS and an IPS?
options: An IDS alerts on threats; an IPS automatically blocks them
An IDS blocks threats; an IPS only alerts
They are the same thing with different names

details.summary: Intrusion detection systems monitor network traffic for suspicious patterns, known attack signatures, and behavioral anomalies that indicate a security breach. IDS alerts security teams to potential threats.
details.whyItMatters: Firewalls block known-bad traffic, but IDS detects attacks that slip through. Without intrusion detection, breaches can persist unnoticed for months, causing far greater damage.
takeaways: IDS monitors traffic for attack signatures and anomalies
IPS can automatically block detected attacks in real time
Network-based and host-based IDS provide different visibility

faq.question: What is the difference between IDS and IPS?
faq.answer: IDS passively monitors and alerts when it detects suspicious activity. IPS sits inline and can automatically block or drop malicious traffic in real time. IPS provides active protection but risks blocking legitimate traffic with false positives. Many deployments use both in complementary roles.

faq.question: How does signature-based detection differ from anomaly-based?
faq.answer: Signature-based detection matches traffic against known attack patterns, like antivirus signatures. It is accurate for known threats but misses new attacks. Anomaly-based detection learns normal behavior and flags deviations. It can catch novel attacks but generates more false positives.
